audits.title: 1333 A Retrospective Audit Against National Standards and Guidelines of The Management and Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis in A London District General Hospital
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines: mortality <10% (<30% severe), diagnosis within 48h, gallbladder ultrasound within 24h, severity stratification within 48h, cause established in >80%, ICU for severe cases, definitive gallstone treatment within 14 days
audits.setting: District general hospital, University Hospital Lewisham, London

cycle1.result: Mortality 2.9% (33.3% in severe); diagnosis within 48h in all; severity stratification 91.2%; aetiology established 82.4%; ultrasound within 24h 41.2%; all severe cases discussed with intensivists; 7.1% of gallstone pancreatitis had definitive treatment within 2 weeks.

audits.intervention: Planned meetings with surgical leads to implement a pathway, with re-audit in 4 months.
audits.other_findings: No weekend ultrasound was available; 50% of those without ultrasound at 24h had CT.
audits.citation: Tytler K, Nip L, Borg C. 1333 A Retrospective Audit Against National Standards and Guidelines of The Management and Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis in A London District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.145.

audits.title: EP.TH.289Diagnosis of the aetiology of acute pancreatitis at a district Hospital: A retrospective audit
audits.standard: NICE NG147: aetiology identified in at least 80%, no more than 20% idiopathic
audits.setting: Surgical assessment unit, district hospital (Pinderfields Hospital)
audits.intervention: Action plan for detailed history and step-wise investigation formulated.
audits.other_findings: Other blood tests often not done in index admission, drug history not elicited, and repeat ultrasound not done.
audits.citation: Ravindran S, Shaaban H, Mohsin M. EP.TH.289Diagnosis of the aetiology of acute pancreatitis at a district Hospital: A retrospective audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab309.037.

audits.title: TH7.9 A retrospective audit of the investigation and management of acute pancreatitis (AP) in a tertiary referral hospital in Ireland
audits.setting: University Hospital Limerick, tertiary referral hospital

cycle1.result: No emergency cholecystectomies; 25.6% (11/43) biliary cases had ERCP and 41.9% referred for outpatient cholecystectomy; 37.2% of alcoholic pancreatitis admissions had cessation advice; 18.6% not fully investigated.

audits.other_findings: No documentation of HbA1c, DEXA or faecal elastase monitoring; a standard operating procedure and re-audit are planned.
audits.citation: Ankatiah S, Julius B, Falusi J, Baban C, Merrigan A, Tormey S. TH7.9 A retrospective audit of the investigation and management of acute pancreatitis (AP) in a tertiary referral hospital in Ireland. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.262.

audits.title: 612 A Quality Improvement Project of Management of Acute Pancreatitis in a District General Hospital; How Well Are We Doing Against NICE Guidelines?
audits.standard: NICE NG104 (cause, antibiotic stewardship, nutrition, severity and complications, lifestyle advice)
audits.setting: Diana Princess of Wales Hospital, district general hospital, Grimsby

cycle1.result: Cause identified 55% (86% within 48 hours); antibiotics 51%, indication recorded in 23%; nil by mouth 91%, reason recorded in 20%; severity documented 6%; lifestyle advice 33%.

audits.intervention: Ongoing: Pancreatitis Management Bundle, local clinical guidelines, staff awareness and patient education (no re-audit reported).
audits.other_findings: Oral nutrition offered in 9% versus 56.4% in the national PANC study; four patients discussed with a tertiary centre.
audits.citation: Scott L, Park J, Revill V. 612 A Quality Improvement Project of Management of Acute Pancreatitis in a District General Hospital; How Well Are We Doing Against NICE Guidelines?. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.252.

audits.title: EP421 - The multidisciplinary management of acute pancreatitis at a district general hospital – an NCEPOD audit

cycle1.result: Cause identified in 70%; 100% of alcoholic pancreatitis referred to alcohol services; nutritional assessment in only 10%; uncontrolled comorbidities not referred onwards.

audits.intervention: MDT teaching sessions and an admission proforma (second loop planned).

audits.title: eP52 Enhancing Acute Pancreatitis Management through a Multidisciplinary Upper Gastrointestinal Team Approach: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: Acute pancreatitis management metrics: Glasgow score within 48 hours, imaging within 24 hours, cholecystectomy within 2 weeks, escalation and referral
audits.setting: Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Escalation of severe cases 0%; cholecystectomy within 2 weeks 75%; transfer of non-gallstone cases to gastroenterology 33%.

audits.intervention: Weekly benign UGI MDT with gastroenterology and radiology, streamlined ERCP pathway, hot cholecystectomy pathway, and targeted surgical education.

cycle2.result: Glasgow score within 48 hours 50%; escalation 60%; imaging within 24 hours 100%; median admission to ERCP 5 days; cholecystectomy within 2 weeks 100%; transfer to gastroenterology 50%.

audits.other_findings: 131 patients were included across both cycles.
audits.citation: Papaioannou C, Soni R, Sheth C, Patwardhan M, Brewer J, Kamocka A. eP52 Enhancing Acute Pancreatitis Management through a Multidisciplinary Upper Gastrointestinal Team Approach: A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae318.039.

audits.title: TTP7.10 Compliance with NCEPOD Guidelines in the Management of Acute Pancreatitis - A Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: NCEPOD recommendations on acute pancreatitis (no early antibiotic prophylaxis; cholecystectomy on index admission for gallstone pancreatitis)
audits.setting: Great Western Hospital; acute pancreatitis admissions

cycle1.result: MRCP/EUS for unclear aetiology 37%; inappropriate antibiotic prophylaxis 42%; previous gallstone admissions 12 (36%); early cholecystectomy 18%.

audits.intervention: Results presented locally; increased 'hot chole' slots and dedicated waiting lists for gallstone pancreatitis.

cycle2.result: MRCP/EUS 48%; inappropriate antibiotic prophylaxis 28%; previous gallstone admissions 5 (16%); early cholecystectomy 31%.

audits.other_findings: Gallstone pancreatitis in 33 (51%) and 32 (48%) patients respectively.
audits.citation: Hussain M, Roberts A, Boyle E, Okkeh O, Chikukuza S, Williamson J, et al.. TTP7.10 Compliance with NCEPOD Guidelines in the Management of Acute Pancreatitis - A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.304.

audits.title: TPTh 9.03 Improving Early Management of Acute Pancreatitis: A Six-Month Audit at Royal Surrey County Hospital
audits.standard: National guidance and WATERFALL trial moderate fluid resuscitation (10ml/kg bolus then 1.5ml/kg/hr), two regular and one PRN analgesic, imaging sequence and Glasgow-Imrie scoring
audits.setting: Royal Surrey County Hospital, adult admissions

cycle1.result: 33% received recommended minimum fluids in 24 hours; 37% had one or no regular analgesic; urine output monitored in 25%; ultrasound first in 25% (CT in 87%); Glasgow-Imrie documented in 12%.

audits.other_findings: A pancreatitis care bundle and re-audit are planned.
audits.citation: Jordanou N, Clarke C. TPTh 9.03 Improving Early Management of Acute Pancreatitis: A Six-Month Audit at Royal Surrey County Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.519.

audits.title: TPTh 9.10 Imaging and Antibiotic Use in Acute Pancreatitis: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Compliance
audits.standard: RCR and UK national guidelines for acute pancreatitis (CT timing, ultrasound within 24 hours, antibiotics)
audits.setting: Chesterfield Royal Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: CT on admission in 43 and within 3 days in 13 more, all with diagnostic amylase, contrary to guidance; ultrasound in 62 at mean 1.9 days (target 24 hours); MRCP in 49 at mean 2.3 days; 22 of 56 given antibiotics without evidence of infection or necrosis.

audits.intervention: Local recommendations implemented and junior teaching started; 2nd cycle planned.
audits.citation: Hanna Y, Gabrawi A, Raizada A, Hope C. TPTh 9.10 Imaging and Antibiotic Use in Acute Pancreatitis: A Retrospective Audit of Guideline Compliance. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.525.

audits.title: TPTh 9.11 Acute Pancreatitis in Surgical Admissions: A Closed- Loop Audit of Compliance Against the British Society of Gastroenterology Guidelines
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for diagnosis, aetiology assessment and risk stratification of acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: General surgery admissions, district general hospital (Wye Valley NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Correct diagnosis within 48 hours 97%; risk stratification within 48 hours 38%; aetiology assessment 62%.

audits.intervention: Results presented at audit meeting, MDT posters and teaching sessions.
audits.other_findings: 5% of cases were deemed idiopathic; risk stratification still below standard.
